scope: HBQ jam cascade/rear observation versus CBE sampled rear support
findings: HBQ distinguishes obstacle back-off from rear-to-front jam requests and uses physics pushes. Preserve bounded room-making intent; do not copy its push executor.
CBE rear observer already adds hull/approach/turn checks, but had no downward support observation.
CBE now samples three longitudinal positions and three hull-width positions, at most nine downward GEOM rays. Missing or steep first supporting surfaces veto native reverse via shared observer.

Bridge geometry can provide support independently of terrain water in the shared observer. Ordinary recovery retains a separate terrain-water/normal destination veto and ground destination; bridge traversal is not accepted.
limits: Discrete samples cannot certify continuous support or thin gaps; native steering changes remain unknown.
Support tolerance is current hull-bottom frame +1.2/-2m and world normal z>=0.7. Modded hull extents, slopes, decks, shorelines and discontinuities require physical validation.
No queue HOLD/READY/reverse/dependency executor exists. Consent is not execution.
At most69 total observer rays; no additional world scan. Runtime overhead unmeasured.
